answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR), filed and dated August 17, 2026; original company statement of the SB Energy residual value guaranty agreements, with the press release referenced as Exhibit 99.1.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own 8-K states that on August 17, 2026 it entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy as Lessor for leases covering about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site (PORTS campus, Pike County, Ohio), with an OpenAI affiliate as tenant. The source supports a contingent, company-reported financial commitment by NVIDIA: if OpenAI's affiliate suffers insolvency causing lease default or fails to pay, NVIDIA pays generally the shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and recoveries from re-leasing or sale. Its initial commitment is cumulatively capped at $105 billion; payments depend on conditions including the Lessor satisfying ready-for-service conditions, expected beginning in 2028. NVIDIA may also provide credit support for about an additional 3.8 GW at its sole discretion. Obligations end at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of lease commencement, lease termination by OpenAI, OpenAI reaching a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary events, and OpenAI has agreed to reimburse amounts NVIDIA actually pays. The agreements are described as effective upon lease commencement. My conditional reading is that NVIDIA is converting a large part of the Portsmouth data center financing and tenant risk into a contingent NVIDIA liability, with the realized cost depending on lease commencement, the 2028 ready-for-service timing, OpenAI's payment and credit standing, and any exercise of the additional 3.8 GW option. The source also says the tenant will use the capacity to deploy NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform, subject to limited exceptions, which is a stated plan rather than a disclosed purchase commitment or order amount.
limitations: The guaranteed minimum value of each lease, the per-lease split of the 4.25 GW, and the expected maximum exposure below the $105 billion cap are not disclosed in the 8-K.

The full text of the Agreements is not in the supplied record; the form will be filed as an exhibit to the 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, so the termination mechanics and reimbursement terms are known only from the summary.
The 2028 ready-for-service timing is the company's stated expectation, not a confirmed date, and no lease commencement has been reported.
Whether and when NVIDIA would exercise the discretionary credit support for about 3.8 GW is not disclosed.
The DSX platform deployment by the OpenAI affiliate is described as planned, with no disclosed quantity, pricing, or purchase commitment from the tenant to NVIDIA.
No NVIDIA revenue, order, or cash flow amount from the Portsmouth Site is disclosed, so the source does not establish direct product sales to the covered company from this arrangement.
The supplied record contains no other source records, historical comparisons, or catalog questions, so consistency with earlier NVIDIA or SB Energy disclosures is unverified.
The OpenAI affiliate's credit standing and the probability of a Trigger Event are not assessed in the source.
follow_up: Retrieve the Exhibit 99.1 press release and the 10-Q exhibit for the quarter ended July 26, 2026 to check the guaranteed minimum values, cap mechanics, and termination terms.
In the next 10-Q and 10-K, check for disclosed guarantee liability, fair value of the guaranty, and any accrual or contingent loss disclosure tied to the Portsmouth Site.
Monitor for lease commencement notices and any SB Energy or OpenAI announcements on ready-for-service status for the Portsmouth Site.
Monitor for any NVIDIA disclosure of exercise of the additional 3.8 GW credit support or any Trigger Event.
Check subsequent NVIDIA filings for any disclosed DSX platform sales or orders tied to the Portsmouth Site.
